newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper adopts near-term upside bias.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper adopts near-term upside bias.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
---------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 21------------
Copper prices have the potential to rechallenge the upside on Monday, but resistance above the $2,300 a tonne area could be a problem, analysts said.
Aluminium looked less vulnerable towards nearby $1,534 support, but lacked upward momentum.
COPPER - A firmer close on Friday might have set up copper to tackle the $2,300 level, which eluded the market's upside attempts last week, analyst said.
But resistance just above, including the April 9 high of $2,313, would likely prove tough going, analysts said.
Short term bullish factors included Friday's price move above the 10-day moving average, currently around $2,280, for the first time in more than two weeks.

A widening of the cash/threes backwardation late last week would also help underpin the market, which was closely watching London Metal Exchange (LME) stock figures for an extension of last week's drawdowns.
Cash/threes was last at a $47/$52 backwardation, compared with $45/$50 at Friday's kerb close.
The market was watching for developments in a small-scale strike at Chile's Escondida mine, which helped boost prices on Friday.
"The union accounts for 17.5 percent of the workforce so work can continue, but should it escalate then output could be affected," analyst William Adams of Rudolf Wolff said in a report.
At 0745 GMT three months copper was indicated at $2,285/87, compared with Friday's kerb close of $2,288.
ALUMINIUM - The market was range trading amid thin volumes, but could follow copper higher.
On the charts, aluminium's RSI of 35 percent and failure to crumble below recent lows was cancelled out by downtrending moving averages, painting a relatively neutral picture, analysts said.

"The fact that the market is becoming oversold argues against prices seriously testing the recent lows around $1,534, but equally upside momentum appears lacking and resistance levels look likely to remain intact in the short term," brokers Brandeis said.
However, a push above resistance in the $1,560-$1,570 area would clear the way to $1,600, analysts noted.
At 0745 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,553/56, versus Friday's kerb close of $1,554.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
